paragraphs: This page builds three separate component families — InputControl, InputField, and a page-level Form wrapper — rather than one cohesive "Form" component.
No component skill exists for this component (form-label-skill.md is an unfilled placeholder). Everything below is derived solely from the actual Figma build.

sections.heading: Shipping address
paragraphs: ① Section heading — labels the field group.
② Field rows — InputField instances, grouped in multi-column rows (name/last-name, city/state/zip) plus a full-width country field.
③ Actions — secondary + primary Button instances.

sections.heading: Variants & States
paragraphs: Three separate component families, each with its own State axis (see Flags for why this is three families rather than one).

sections.heading: Behaviour
paragraphs: InputControl is the bare field; InputField adds a label, helper, and validation message row; Form composes multiple InputField rows with a heading and Cancel/Submit actions, plus page-level submission states (Submitting/Success/Error/Disabled).

Missing tier-1 skill: form-label-skill.md is a bare placeholder, so nothing below has a documented spec to verify against.

Unexplained variant name: InputControl includes a state literally named "State9" (bold/red above) alongside otherwise-sensible names (Default, Hover, Focused, Filled, Disabled, Read-only, Error, Success). This reads as an auto-generated Figma default that was never renamed — flagged for follow-up rather than guessed at.

Possible page overlap with ↳ Input: this page's InputControl and InputField closely resemble (and may duplicate) the Input component built on the separate ↳ Input page — both represent a single-line field with an overlapping state vocabulary. Nothing documents whether these are intentionally distinct or an unintentional duplicate build.

No Do's/Don'ts section: with no source skill, there is no documented rule to visualize.
